question.text: A manager forecasts correctly on 60 out of 80 quarterly predictions in a year. What is the manager's Information Coefficient?

explanation.text: The Logic: IC = 2 × (Right predictions / Total predictions) − 1 = 2 × (60/80) − 1 = 2 × 0.75 − 1 = 0.50. The Trap: 0.75 is the raw hit ratio (Right/Total) before applying the IC formula. 0.25 drops a factor; 0.60 is noise. Note: The formula IC = 2 × (Right/Total) − 1 is the workbook's standard definition and is applied in the same way in the sample caselets.
